summary: Independent review of the Webull closing-only open-latch. THE CAUSE WAS SETTLED BY THE OPERATOR, NOT BY INFERENCE: he placed a BDRX order by hand in the Webull UI and received the human-readable form of the code we were getting — 'This symbol is restricted to closing orders only.' That resolves the ambiguity I had flagged and is better evidence than the nine log events could ever have provided. Population confirmed independently: CAN_NOT_CREATE_A_OPEN_ORDER has occurred on EXACTLY TWO symbols in all history, WHLR (2026-08-28) and BDRX (2026-09-11, eight times 11:39-12:14 with the price falling 1.3647 -> 1.2273 as we chased it), and NEITHER has ever filled on live:orb on any day. I also ruled out the alternatives by measurement before accepting the symbol-level explanation: ORDER SHAPE is identical (BDRX rejected and FTFT accepted were both STOP_LIMIT, qty 1, day); PRICE is refuted at every band (live:orb has filled 107 buys under , and 14 STOP_LIMIT buys under .50); and ACCOUNT/VENUE STATE is refuted by timing (FTFT FILLED on the same Webull account at 12:02, inside the BDRX rejection window). THE SAFETY PROPERTY THAT MATTERS AND IS PINNED: 'restricted to closing orders only' means Webull STILL ACCEPTS SELLS, so the latch must suppress OPENS ONLY — latching the symbol wholesale while holding a position would block our own exit, which is strictly worse than the rejects it prevents. Mutations, correctly targeted after one partial attempt of mine: making the latch also block closes -> test_a_rejected_close_can_never_create_the_open_only_latch fails RED; dropping the CAN_NOT_CREATE_A_OPEN_ORDER code from the matcher -> 3 controls fail; dropping the 'restricted to closing orders only' UI wording -> 1 control fails; and disabling the WHOLE transient exclude list -> 2 controls fail including test_429_veto_wins_even_with_a_not_tradable_substring, so the operator's 2026-07-24 conservatism (a rate-limit or timeout must NEVER latch a symbol) survives this change intact. ⚠ METHOD NOTE: my first attempt at that last mutation replaced only the FIRST entry of the exclude tuple and survived meaninglessly; neutering the whole tuple turns it red. An incomplete mutation is not a surviving mutant. Controlled full unit pair vs base 2fae102: base 46 failed/3606 passed, head 46 failed/3612 passed, ZERO new failure names and ZERO fixed. Ruff clean. Ancestor PASS. Reviewer differs from the author. ⚠ COST CONTEXT for sequencing, unchanged: ZERO dollars — Schwab also refuses BDRX ('must be placed with a broker'), so there was never a trade to lose on either broker. This is noise and reject-ceiling pressure and correctly sits last in the queue. No findings; nothing withheld.
